key_insight: ACE-Data-0 proposes a human-centric ambient capture system that records the full embodied experience of people in real home environments, linking perception, motion, manipulation, sound, and touch over time. The key idea is to turn everyday activity into a richer data engine for embodied AI.
problem_solved: Embodied AI is limited by fragmented datasets that separately capture viewpoints, modalities, or scales, making it hard to learn the full perception-action loop and how humans pursue goals in the real world.
method: Introduces the Ambient Capture Engine (ACE), a human-centric data pipeline for collecting multimodal embodied data in natural home settings.
Captures synchronized first-person perception, whole-body motion, dexterous hand actions, object state changes, audio, and tactile cues across time.
Organizes the data to preserve temporal relationships between sensing and action, enabling downstream learning of complete human activity episodes.
impact: This matters because embodied models need realistic, temporally aligned data to learn robust world understanding and action policies. For practitioners, ACE-Data-0 can support better training, evaluation, and benchmarking for robotics, AR/VR, and human-AI interaction systems.

paper_title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
paper_authors: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Beichen Wen, Runmao Yao, Yinghao Liu
